as_is.description: Faithful reconstruction of what the pinned foxBMS sources demonstrate. Records observed behavior, existing artifacts/tests, justified inferences, evidence gaps, contradictions, and proposed changes. Does not rewrite inconvenient facts or assert undocumented original stakeholder intent. Back-inferred requirements labeled as reconstructed behavior descriptions, not historical approved specifications.

synthetic_reference.description: Complete, coherent hypothetical automotive BMS development project grounded in foxBMS. Defines fictional item, vehicle context, operating assumptions, selected hardware/software baseline, stakeholders, responsibilities, lifecycle, and parameter set. Reuses source-grounded behavior where justified. Fills missing engineering content with labeled synthetic requirements, analyses, design additions, process records, and test fixtures.

provenance_rules.source_observed: Directly from foxBMS sources with durable anchors
provenance_rules.derived: Logical inference from source_observed premises with reasoning
provenance_rules.synthetic: Explicitly created to fill gaps, labeled with rationale and validity conditions

synthetic_reference.scope: Hypothetical automotive BMS project using foxBMS as reference platform

rules.description: Never renumber established IDs when inserting records
Identify exact revisions on baseline-controlled links
An artefact identifier is unique WITHIN ITS PROFILE. Two records of different profiles may legitimately carry the same identifier string, and doing so is conformant, not a collision and not a defect.

amended.author: safety_engineer
amended.previous_text: IDs must be globally unique across profiles
amended.previous_meaning: The identifier string alone identified a record across the whole corpus. A string carried by two records was a policy violation, whether or not the two records were about the same subject, and repairing it required re-issuing one of the two under ID-RULE-003.
amended.new_meaning: The pair (profile, id) identifies a record. Uniqueness is required and enforced inside one profile; two records of different profiles may share a string, and that sharing is a permitted state. The pair (profile, id) is therefore the corpus's primary key, and a reference that supplies only the id does not yet resolve.
amended.supersedes: The corpus-wide-uniqueness reading of ID-RULE-004 as previously written, i.e. the single sentence 'IDs must be globally unique across profiles' in its entirety. It does not supersede ID-RULE-001, ID-RULE-002 or ID-RULE-003, which are unchanged and continue to govern renumbering, endpoint revision labelling and supersession/deletion/migration respectively.
rationale: This is route (b) of the two the corpus itself put forward in FB2-SAF-VOC-000001 at identifier_vocabulary.migration_decision_2026_10_03.why_the_migration_was_still_not_performed and in CORR-COV-021.governance_question_referred, and it is the route the amendment adopts.

The amended rule describes what the tool already enforces. `_validate_no_duplicate_ids` keys on (profile, id) and reports a duplicate only within one profile; the link validator resolves both endpoints as (profile, id); every id-keyed lookup in corpus.py has resolved as a pair since the corpus was first indexed. Under the previous text the corpus was in permanent, declared non-conformance with itself: the policy asserted a property the enforcing code did not implement and could not implement without a migration of roughly nine hundred prose references. The amendment makes the policy and the corpus agree by amending the policy, which is the direction that changes no engineering content.

The alternative, amending nothing and migrating under ID-RULE-003, was measured and declined on the evidence recorded in that same entry: renaming the synthetic_reference side would not make the roughly nine hundred unqualified prose references correct, it would make them resolve to the as_is copy while still reading as though they meant the synthetic one, and no validator would fire because every renamed identifier would still resolve to exactly one live record. That converts a two-candidate ambiguity into a confidently wrong reference, which is the worse failure.

Thirty-nine identifier strings are currently each carried by two records, one per profile, and `origin` disagrees on all thirty-nine pairs, so they are thirty-nine pairs of distinct subjects rather than thirty-nine duplicate records. Under the amended rule all thirty-nine are conformant and require no repair.

The amendment does not make reference ambiguity disappear. It relocates it: it makes (profile, id) the key, and it leaves the corpus's existing convention - an unqualified id is read as the synthetic_reference copy - as the thing that resolves the remainder. That convention is now load-bearing under this rule rather than merely convenient, and the residual risk it creates is the subject of the detector named in detection_consequence below.
consequences_recorded_here_not_silently_: NO RENAME IS REQUIRED OR PERMITTED for the 39 shared identifier strings. They are conformant under the amended rule. Any future proposal to re-issue them must cite this amendment and explain why a conformant state is being disturbed.

The 'Do not renumber' sentence in FB2-SAF-VOC-000001 identifier_vocabulary.adopted_convention cited ID-RULE-001 and read as though a rename were unavailable. That reasoning is superseded: the rename was never blocked by ID-RULE-001, it was declined on the reference-convention evidence. The two documents formerly disagreed and now do not; the reconciliation is recorded at FB2-SAF-VOC-000001 identifier_vocabulary.supersession_reconciliation_2026_10_04.
ID-RULE-003 is NOT invoked by this amendment. No supersession, deletion or migration is being performed, so the instrument this rule provides is not the one in play.

RESIDUAL RISK, now the primary one: approximately nine hundred prose references name an artefact identifier with no profile qualifier, and the corpus adopts the convention that an unqualified id means the synthetic_reference copy. That convention is what resolves them. Where the named id is carried by more than one live record, the convention supplies the answer and a reader who does not know it has two live candidates and no way to choose. corpus.py detects this as reference ambiguity, reported and not gated; it is not an identifier-collision finding, because under this rule there are no identifier collisions.
amended.detection_consequence: corpus.py's former cross-profile identifier reuse finding is withdrawn as a violation, because the condition it reported is conformant under this amendment. It is replaced by an ambiguity detector for unqualified references that name an id carried by more than one live record. Severity is report-only: no machine-read path is currently ambiguous, because every id-keyed lookup resolves (profile, id).
amended.scope_and_limits: This amendment changes the corpus policy text and its meaning. It does not rename anything, does not revise any artefact's engineering content, does not assert ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level, human approval, production authorisation or product verification credit, and does not close any coverage dimension. Every record touched by this amendment keeps human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false.

required_relations.note: Applicable when validation against stakeholder needs is in scope

parameter_registry.description: Single coherent parameter registry: units, tolerances, domains, sign conventions, timing budgets, thresholds, hysteresis, debounce, calibration, configuration selection, assumptions.
parameter_registry.governance: Parameters defined once, referenced by ID. No scattered conflicting hard-coded values.

execution_kind.description: Orthogonal to outcome. Planning is not execution. Fabricated simulation-looking numbers are synthetic_fixture.

outcome.description: Actual test results or synthetic fixture expectations

rules: Actual simulation run requires executed model and captured logs
Missing target hardware or proprietary compilers = blocked, not fabricated success
Generated consistency-check results validate the corpus, not the BMS product

review_policy.batch_review_rules: Only when all covered IDs/digests and findings enumerated
review_policy.ai_review_limitations: AI reviews are automated reviews. Distinct agent sessions are not organizational independence or human confirmation measures. Real human approval remains pending.

approval_ledger_amendment.author: safety_engineer
approval_ledger_amendment.previous_text: Element 6 of the APPROVAL-RULE-A1 evidence contract, at docs/artifacts/governance/role-and-review-policy.json#/approval_evidence_contract/required_elements[5]: '6. a revision_history entry whose author is the approving role, whose revision is at least the record's current revision, and whose description both records the approval and references the signed packet by digest or by path'. Element 5 of the same contract accepted a cited packet from either docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ or docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/, and every generated review packet instructed the reviewer to archive the signed packet under reviews/signed/ as guidance rather than as a rule, because both locations resolved. Staleness had no state at all: when a record's bytes changed, the approval's attested record digest stopped matching and the approval simply stopped counting, with no signal that a human judgement had been invalidated.
approval_ledger_amendment.previous_meaning: Element 6 made an approval a CONTENT CHANGE, which it is not. A revision_history entry is by definition a statement that the record's content moved, so recording an approval through one forces the revision to bump; a bumped revision stales every link that pins that record's revision AND invalidates the sha256 that every review record stores for it. Measured, not assumed, in closing-list.md 1.6 P3 and coverage-plan.json CORR-COV-022 residual risk 4. So a properly evidenced approval could not be recorded at all without collateral damage, and the corpus papered over it with an unratified workaround: record the approval against the CURRENT revision. The tell was the tool's own happy-path self-test, which had to pick a record that NO review digest covers in order to prove the approval validated at all - the signature of an unsatisfiable requirement being demonstrated rather than an unsatisfiable one being stated. Element 5's two-root acceptance meant the archive rule was advisory: nothing stopped a reviewer citing a packet in the regenerated tree, where the evidence would be destroyed by the next regeneration and the approval would fail element 5 for a reason that had nothing to do with the reviewer's judgement. And staleness was invisible: an invalidated human judgement produced no finding, no count and no state - only a numerator that quietly stopped moving.
approval_ledger_amendment.new_rule: APPROVALS ARE EVENTS, NOT CONTENT. Element 6 is replaced. An approval is recorded by appending one JSON object to the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl, carrying ledger_id, record_id, profile, kind, approved_record_sha256 (the CONTENT digest of the record at signing), approved_content_revision, approved_by, role, independence, date, signed_packet{path,sha256}, packet_first_commit and previous_entry_sha256. The record keeps exactly one thing: approval_ledger_ref, naming its ledger entry. approval_ledger_ref is APPROVAL METADATA, not content - it is excluded from the content digest, it is never a revision_history entry, and recording it does not bump the record's revision. The content digest of a record is the sha256 of its bytes with approval metadata removed, so a record carrying no approval_ledger_ref - all 321 of them today - has content digest equal to its file-byte sha256 and every one of the 261 stored review digests still verifies. The review-digest check compares the CONTENT digest. Therefore recording an approval neither stales a link nor invalidates a review digest, and a self-test performs the whole recording on a throwaway tree and asserts exactly that. Element 5 is tightened: a cited packet is admissible ONLY from docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/; a citation into docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ is REJECTED with a message saying the signed packet must be archived first, because that tree is regenerated. Staleness becomes a first-class measured state: an entry whose approved_record_sha256 no longer matches is STALE, which is NOT invalid - it does not fail validation - and is reported and counted in the new approval_staleness metric as stale/total, in a finding that names the record, the ledger entry and the fields that changed, recoverable because every signed packet embeds the approved record verbatim under record_verbatim so the validator diffs approved bytes against current bytes rather than printing two opaque digests. A stale approval is excluded from the human_approval numerator, because that numerator means 'records carrying an approval that describes the bytes now on disk'; it is not discarded, because human_approval and approval_staleness together account for every approval in the ledger. Elements 1-5, the independence rule and the production-authority bar are unchanged.
approval_ledger_amendment.new_meaning: Recording an approval is now a free act with respect to every other control: it does not bump a revision, does not stale a link, and does not invalidate a review digest, because the corpus can finally tell the difference between a record's content and a statement about that content. Two further consequences follow. First, the archive rule is now a rule rather than a suggestion, so a signed packet cannot be parked in a tree that regeneration would overwrite. Second, an invalidated human judgement is now VISIBLE: approval_staleness reads stale/total on every coverage run and a finding names what changed, so 'your approval of X no longer describes X' is said at the moment it becomes true rather than discovered months later.
approval_ledger_amendment.supersedes: Element 6 of APPROVAL-RULE-A1 as written - the revision_history requirement - in its entirety. That element is WITHDRAWN, not deleted: its text is preserved at role-and-review-policy.json#/approval_evidence_contract/required_elements[5] and the reason for withdrawing it at .../approval_ledger_contract/element_6_withdrawal_reason. Also superseded: the two-root admissibility of element 5 (docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ is no longer admissible) and the implicit convention, recorded as open P3 in closing-list.md 1.6, that an approval is recorded against the record's current revision. Nothing else is superseded. Elements 1-5 of APPROVAL-RULE-A1, the independence_rule, the production-authority bar, APPROVAL-RULE-A1 in its entirety, the recursive authority_keys scan, the four GOVERNANCE_CLAIM_FIELDS claim classes, acceptance gate [7/8], the provenance gate and the packet generator's no-written-signature rule are all unchanged, and self-tests assert each of the ones that could plausibly have been affected.
approval_ledger_amendment.residual_limit_that_this_does_not_reduce: THE HASH CHAIN PROVES EXISTENCE, ORDERING AND INTEGRITY. THE GIT ANCHOR PROVES WHEN AND IN WHAT STATE THE PACKET WAS COMMITTED. NEITHER PROVES THAT A HUMAN READ ANYTHING, AND NONE OF THIS MAKES AN APPROVAL UNFORGEABLE. A determined person can still write all six elements, archive a packet, cite a real commit and maintain the chain correctly, and nothing in this repository can distinguish that from an approval a competent independent reviewer genuinely gave. This limit is IRREDUCIBLE - any attestation can be forged by someone determined to lie. What this amendment did is raise the COST of forgery (six elements, each independently sufficient to obstruct it; a chain every entry is bound to; an anchor into version history) and make forgery DETECTABLE after the fact (the first chain break is reported by name). Neither of those is prevention. Nothing in this repository, in this amendment or in any other should be described as making approval unforgeable.
approval_ledger_amendment.detection_consequence: New rules, all currently unreachable because the ledger holds zero entries: approval_ledger_malformed, approval_ledger_entry_incomplete, approval_ledger_duplicate_id, approval_ledger_chain_broken (reports the FIRST break only, by entry index and ledger_id), approval_ledger_record_unresolved, approval_ledger_anchor_commit_unknown, approval_ledger_anchor_blob_absent, approval_ledger_ref_unresolved and approval_approval_stale. The last is MEDIUM severity and non-gating by design: a stale approval is a measured state, not an invalid record, so it must never make validate fail or turn the suite red. Everything else is high. The review-digest check now compares the CONTENT digest rather than the raw file digest; for every one of the 321 records this is identical to the raw digest, because none carries approval metadata, so the provenance tally reads exactly as it did before (261 verified, 0 placeholder, 0 mismatch). _validate_governance_semantics parity is preserved: element 6 lives inside the same _approval_evidence_defects predicate that both _validate_artifact and the gate reach, so gate [7/8] cannot go blind to a ledger fabrication, and a self-test asserts that a ledger-ref defect is reported once through each path.
what_this_does_not_do: IT DOES NOT RECORD AN APPROVAL. The ledger is empty and every record keeps human_approval_status pending, production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false. Making the gate accept a legitimately evidenced approval is what makes the guard meaningful; producing one needs a person, and no code path in this repository may do it.
IT DOES NOT ADD ANY AUTHORITY TO ANYONE. The corpus still asserts no ASIL determination, no ISO 26262 conformity, no certification, no production authorisation and no product verification credit.

IT DOES NOT CLOSE A COVERAGE DIMENSION. All fifteen dimensions hold their values; human_approval stays 0/321, production_authorization 0/321, actual_product_evidence 0/33. approval_staleness is added as an explicitly counted METRIC in the coverage output rather than as a sixteenth dimension, so that 'fifteen dimensions' remains a true statement about this corpus and the staleness figure is still reported on every run.
IT DOES NOT FIX FORGERY. See residual_limit_that_this_does_not_reduce. The honest claim is cost and detectability, not prevention.
IT DOES NOT RELAX human_approval_status 'not_required'. Still rejected for want of evidence; still open P3 in closing-list.md 1.6.

IT DOES NOT WEAKEN ANY OTHER CONTROL. The recursive authority-key scan, the four claim classes, acceptance gate [7/8], the provenance gate, the packet verifier and the generator's no-written-signature rule are untouched, and self-tests assert each of the ones that could plausibly have been affected.
approval_ledger_amendment.scope_and_limits: This amendment changes docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py (element 6, element 5 admissibility, a content digest, the ledger loader and chain validator, the staleness metric and its findings, and new self-tests), docs/artifacts/tools/make_review_packets.py (the signature section of all 321 packets and what --transcribe prints), all 321 generated packets and their 321 packet.json twins, docs/artifacts/governance/role-and-review-policy.json (a new approval_ledger_contract block; APPROVAL-RULE-A1 left byte-for-byte intact), docs/artifacts/governance/corpus-policy.json (this block), docs/artifacts/governance/coverage-plan.json (correction CORR-COV-023), docs/artifacts/governance/closing-list.md, docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/README.md, and it creates docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl (EMPTY) and approval-ledger.md. It renames no artefact, revises no artefact's engineering content, writes no approval value into any record, appends no ledger entry, asserts no ISO 26262 conformity, no certification, no tool qualification, no ASPICE capability level, no human approval, no production authorisation and no product verification credit, and closes no coverage dimension.

approval_rule_amendment.author: safety_engineer
approval_rule_amendment.previous_text: In docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py _validate_artifact, three rules failed validation on the VALUE alone, with no further test of any kind: 'production_authorized must be false (synthetic corpus)' (production_authorized_rejected, critical); 'human_approval_status must remain pending (no human approval performed)' (human_approval_rejected, high); 'product_verification_credit must be false' (verification_credit_rejected, high). _validate_governance_semantics independently reported the same three fields as governance_authority_claim, so acceptance gate [7/8] failed on them too. The two coverage dimensions human_approval and production_authorization were the literal {"numerator": 0} in _coverage_dimensions, with the detail strings 'all artifacts pending human approval (none performed)' and 'production_authorized=false for all artifacts (by policy)', and the coverage report's basis table classified both as 'constant'.
approval_rule_amendment.previous_meaning: An approval value was forbidden unconditionally. The rule could not distinguish a fabricated approval from a legitimate one because it never inspected one; it could say only 'no', never 'this one is unsigned'. The corpus therefore had exactly two reachable states for approval - absent and forbidden - and no way to represent the legitimate middle. A reviewer who had done the work had nowhere to record it, and the first signature would have turned the acceptance suite red and been blamed for it. Separately, the two coverage dimensions measured nothing: a literal numerator reads 0/321 before any signature exists and would read 0/321 after three hundred, so the figure could not distinguish 'no approvals' from 'the dimension is not implemented', while its detail strings asserted a measured fact that nothing in the function had looked at.
approval_rule_amendment.new_rule: An approval value is NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. Each of the three rules now fires unless the record itself carries, under approval_evidence.<kind>, all six elements enumerated at docs/artifacts/governance/role-and-review-policy.json#/approval_evidence_contract/required_elements: (1) the grant value; (2) approved_by, a named individual rather than a role or a team; (3) role, a role_id declared in that same policy, plus an independence object carrying owner_role equal to the record's own owner_role, satisfied true, a non-placeholder evidence string and a policy_ref, with independence ENFORCED - the approving role must differ from owner_role and from the author of the last revision_history entry that changed the record's content; (4) an ISO-8601 date, grammar- and parse-checked; (5) review_packet carrying path, sha256 and record_sha256_at_signing, where the path resolves to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/packets/ or docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/, the sha256 equals that file's bytes as they stand now, record_sha256_at_signing equals the cited packet's OWN integrity.record_sha256, and the packet's target.record_id and target.profile both name this record; (6) a revision_history entry whose author is the approving role, whose revision is at least the record's current revision, and whose description records the approval and cites the signed packet. Each finding names which element is unmet. production_authorization additionally requires the approving role to be one the corpus grants production authority to and the record's artefact family to be one human approval is required for, so its bar is strictly higher rather than the same bar twice. The two coverage dimensions are now computed from the records by the same predicate the validator enforces.
approval_rule_amendment.new_meaning: The corpus may now record a human approval, and `corpus.py check` stays green when it does - but only a properly evidenced one. The guard against fabrication is no longer the absence of the value; it is a digest chain that binds a signature to a named person, a declared role, an enforced independence relation, a date, one specific packet file and one specific state of one specific record. An approval that is real but unevidenced fails; an approval that is evidenced but not real still requires a person to have lied, and the evidence of that is public. The coverage dimensions read 0 because nothing is approved, and they now say so as a measurement rather than as a convention.
approval_rule_amendment.supersedes: The blanket prohibition in corpus.py for the three rules human_approval_rejected, production_authorized_rejected and verification_credit_rejected, i.e. each rule's failure on the value alone, in its entirety; and the same three fields' unconditional failure in _validate_governance_semantics as governance_authority_claim. It supersedes nothing else. In particular it does NOT supersede the recursive authority_keys scan (production_release, production_approval, safety_approval, authorized_for_production, approved_for_production, release_approved, production_sign_off, production_authority, production_release_approved), the four GOVERNANCE_CLAIM_FIELDS claim classes (ASIL determination, conformity, certification), acceptance gate [7/8], the provenance gate, or the packet generator's rule that no code path writes a signature. All are unchanged.
rationale: The instrument was wrong, not merely strict. A rule that fails on the value alone cannot examine an approval, so it cannot tell a fabricated one from a real one. It made the legitimate state unrepresentable and, in doing so, taught a reviewer that the corpus had no way to accept their work.

A ban has the further defect that it cannot degrade gracefully. There were only two states, so the corpus could not record partial progress: a reviewer who had reviewed 40 records had nowhere to put that fact.

Replacing the value test with an evidence requirement does not merely move the line; it makes each of the six elements a separate, independently sufficient obstacle to fabrication. A script that writes 'approved' still fails at element 1. One that copies a plausible block still fails at element 5 unless a real packet exists whose own recorded record digest is the digest attested. One that has a real packet still fails at element 3 unless the approver is independent of both the owner role and the content author.

The six-element check was read from role-and-review-policy.json rather than restated in the tool, following the pattern ID-RULE-004-A1 set the day before: a policy the enforcing code does not read is a policy that can drift, and this corpus has already corrected one such drift by amending the policy to match the code.

The production-authority bar is strictly higher because the existing code already treats production authority as a different claim from approval: it reports it at critical rather than high severity, it excludes production_authorized from its own authority_keys scan precisely because the named check owns it, and role-and-review-policy.json already separates roles with release authority (architect, safety_manager) from roles that merely review. Reusing that distinction is stricter than inventing a bar, and inventing one would have been a governance decision nobody took.

Both dimensions are computed by the validator's own predicate. Writing a second, looser notion of 'approved' inside _coverage_dimensions would have produced a figure that could read higher than the gate permits, which is the same class of defect as the literal: a number that cannot be wrong.

The amendment was proved in both directions before it was accepted: six rejection cases assert that everything the prohibition caught is still caught, and one acceptance case asserts that a properly evidenced approval really does pass. The acceptance case runs entirely against a throwaway copy of the tree outside the repository and asserts afterwards that nothing was persisted. A rule change that only asserted the rejections would have passed against the old ban unchanged and proved nothing.
what_this_does_not_do: IT DOES NOT PRODUCE AN APPROVAL. No record in this corpus carries one, before or after this amendment. Making the gate accept a legitimately evidenced approval is what makes the guard meaningful; producing such an approval needs a person, and the self-test 'no record in the corpus carries an approval of any kind' fails the suite if one ever appears.

IT DOES NOT ADD ANY AUTHORITY TO ANYONE. The corpus still asserts no ASIL determination, no ISO 26262 conformity, no certification, no production authorisation and no product verification credit. Every record keeps production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false.

IT DOES NOT RELAX human_approval_status 'not_required'. That value is not an approval, the contract does not speak to it, and it continues to fail for want of evidence - preserving the pre-amendment verdict rather than changing it as a side effect. Recorded as an open P3 in closing-list.md §1.6.

IT DOES NOT WEAKEN ANY OTHER CONTROL. The recursive authority-key scan, the four claim classes, acceptance gate [7/8], the provenance gate, the packet verifier and the generator's no-written-signature rule are all untouched, and self-tests assert each of the ones that could plausibly have been affected.

IT IS NOT A ROUTE TO CLOSING A COVERAGE DIMENSION BY AUTHORING. The human_approval numerator can only move by a properly evidenced approval, which requires a signed packet, which requires a person who read the record.
residual_risks_recorded_here_not_silentl: A DETERMINED HUMAN CAN STILL FORGE ALL SIX ELEMENTS. The digest chain proves a packet exists and pins the record state it was generated against. It does not prove anybody read anything. What is left is that the evidence is public, checkable and attributable, and that the batch record must name who signed what.

reviews/signed/ IS AN ORDINARY DIRECTORY. No control signs it. A signed packet there is protected by the generator's refusal to overwrite a signed packet in packets/ and by the validator's refusal to accept a digest that no longer matches, not by any cryptographic control over the archive. Whether signed/ is the only permitted home is an open P2.

IF A RECORD LEGITIMATELY CHANGES AFTER BEING APPROVED, THE APPROVAL STOPS VALIDATING. That is intended - the signature covered specific bytes - but it means an approval is not durable across a content change, and a reviewer must be told so. Every regenerated packet says so.

AN APPROVAL THAT BUMPS THE REVISION NUMBER CANNOT BE RECORDED WITHOUT BREAKING OTHER CONTROLS. Measured, not assumed: bumping it makes every link pinning that record's revision stale and invalidates the sha256 every review record stores for it. The contract therefore records the approval against the CURRENT revision. This convention is implemented and documented but NOT ratified as policy - open P3 in closing-list.md §1.6.
approval_rule_amendment.detection_consequence: The three rule ids are unchanged, so every scenario, gate and report that counts them keeps counting the same quantity. What changes is their meaning and their message: each now enumerates the unmet elements instead of asserting that a value is forbidden. Three findings move rule attribution - a bare production_authorized, human_approval_status or product_verification_credit grant is now reported under production_authorized_rejected / human_approval_rejected / verification_credit_rejected rather than governance_authority_claim - and all three ids are members of GOVERNANCE_SEMANTIC_RULE_IDS, so the violation COUNT printed by gate [7/8] is unchanged. One finding is reported per (rule, artefact) even though cmd_validate runs both _validate_artifact and _validate_governance_semantics over the same index, so the count cannot be inflated by the delegation.
approval_rule_amendment.scope_and_limits: This amendment changes the corpus tool's approval rules, the two approval coverage dimensions, the review packet generator's instructions to reviewers, and the governance text in closing-list.md and role-and-review-policy.json. It renames no artefact, revises no artefact's engineering content, writes no approval value into any record, asserts no ISO 26262 conformity, no certification, no tool qualification, no ASPICE capability level, no production authorisation and no product verification credit, and closes no coverage dimension. Every record touched keeps human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, exactly as ID-RULE-004-A1 required of itself.
